_how: The Primary Digital Cognition Curriculum (The EdTech Playbook, Figure 4.3), Mark Anderson's own wording. Shown on the home page under Where IDEAL Thinkers comes from.

strands.name: Digital Citizenship
ks1: Understanding basic online safety rules
Creating safe online profiles
Understanding appropriate online behaviour
Basic understanding of ownership of digital content
Recognising the importance of keeping information private
ks2: Recognising online risks and knowing how to report issues
Managing digital footprints and online reputation
Understanding cyberbullying and how to address it
Understanding copyright, fair use, and Creative Commons
Creating strong passwords and recognising phishing scams
Understanding deep fakes and AI in TV, media, and social media

strands.name: Digital Literacy
ks1: Basic skills in using digital devices
Simple content creation (e.g., digital drawing, use of the camera etc.)
Identifying reliable sources and basic searching
Using digital platforms to share ideas
Understanding polite online communication
ks2: Proficient use of a variety of digital tools and software
Creating and editing multimedia content (e.g., presentations, videos)
Evaluating the credibility of online information and effective searching
Collaborating on projects using online tools
Practising respectful and constructive online communication
Knowing how to use technology to support learning

strands.name: Computer Science
ks1: Introduction to simple programming languages (e.g., ScratchJr)
Understanding simple algorithms (e.g., sequences)
Understanding what data is and simple ways to represent it
Basic understanding of how computers connect and communicate
Developing problem-solving skills through patterns
ks2: Developing programs using visual languages (e.g., Scratch)
Designing and debugging programs using logical reasoning
Using data structures such as arrays and tables
Exploring internet safety and how the web works
Applying computational thinking to solve complex problems

strands.name: AI Literacy
ks1: Understanding what AI is
Identifying common AI applications (e.g., voice assistants)
Basic understanding of ethical behaviour with AI tools
Simple AI games and activities
Creating AI images using simple tools
ks2: Basic concepts of machine learning and algorithms
Exploring real-world AI applications in various fields
Discussing bias in AI and its implications
Creating basic AI projects and experiments
Learning prompt crafting for AI tools
Understanding the role of AI in automating tasks and enhancing productivity
Ethical considerations, including AI bias and transparency
